numbers.name: term_map

numbers.name: threshold_saturating_uptake
numbers.value: Monod uptake at 20 random parameter sets: S = 1.3 S* persists, S = 0.7 S* washes out (full integration), so S* = delta R*_min does not need linear uptake

numbers.name: steady_abundance
numbers.value: n* = Y (S0 - R*) and R = R* at 20 random sets (rel < 1e-6)

numbers.name: linear_limit
numbers.value: mu = a R: chemostat integrator equals the action-derived layer 3 integrator and n* = (S - delta R*)/(a F R*) at 20 random sets (rel < 1e-6)

numbers.name: exclusion
numbers.value: two consumers at 20 random sets: the lower-R* consumer remains, the other falls below 1e-6 of it, R -> R*_min (rel < 1e-4)

note: Derivation and numerical check; the four S* values are R* from Tilman (1977) Table 1 (registered data of Test Card T007) times D = 0.25 per day, not a comparison with an outcome. In a chemostat the supply that the parent action leaves open (C_L3_SUPPLY) is the product of two quantities the experimenter sets, the dilution rate and the reservoir concentration, and the threshold S* = delta R*_min holds for any increasing uptake with mu(0) = 0. With two essential resources a diatom persists only if both supply fluxes exceed its thresholds. Nearest known theory: chemostat theory (Monod 1950; Novick and Szilard 1950) and Tilman's R* rule. Not UET-distinct.
